notes: Here is one property of the detector. Whatever came before, if the final pair rises, the last output is one. This is one implication, corresponding to thesis Eq1.14, rather than the fuller Eq1.13 behaviour. It does not cover the non-rising case, the initial sample or correctness of generated hardware. The waveform illustrates the requirement and is not a simulation proof.
The initial state st is arbitrary. Connect the quantified mathematical st to the state binder st in the full dependent type.
The earlier inputs xs and final inputs x and y are arbitrary. The prefix can be any list. The variables are bound separately; the last two inputs do not replace the arbitrary prefix.

We take evidence of the unsigned comparison result as an assumption: bvLtu x y equals BV 1. Follow the rising premise in the proposition, the p_ltu evidence parameter and the waveform condition. Do not silently assume a proof of the external primitive implementation.

The result contains an output prefix ys together with evidence about the complete output. Explain the dependent pair ** as an output prefix together with evidence. The witness ys is a value; the equality is its associated evidence.
This is the Idris2/software interpretation of the model, initialised with st. The equality states what this interpretation yields, rather than the correctness of arbitrary generated hardware.
Its input is the arbitrary prefix followed by x and y: xs ++ [x] ++ [y]. Follow the input guide back to the waveform. Preserve the sequence order and unsigned comparison.

Its output must end in one: ys ++ [BV 1]. This establishes the stated rising implication only, not its converse or the non-rising case. Transition: The abstract model also has implementation interpretations. We will return to the proof of this property after showing that connection. Technical grounding: thesis Eq1.13–1.14 and Figure1.6(a), pp26–28. No new standalone proof or generated-hardware correctness is claimed here.
